Back
Getting started
Sign up

Create an account with an email and password, then confirm the verification email flashkarte sends you. Your decks and study progress are tied to that account and sync across every device you sign in on — this app and the web.
The loop

flashkarte has one core loop: write a deck, then study it. New cards are marked New; once a card has been studied, spaced repetition decides when it is due again. Studying regularly, even briefly, is what makes the schedule work.
Where things are
Decks — your decks, with due counts and quick actions to study, share, or delete.
Library — search public decks shared by other users and clone one into your account.
Settings — account, appearance, AI connection, and data.
Writing decks
Three ways to create a deck
Tap the + button on Decks to create or import a deck using the format below.
On the web, use the deck editor with the same Markdown format.
Let an AI assistant build a deck for you — see Creating decks with AI below.
The format
A deck is plain Markdown. The first heading is the title. Use second-level headings to group cards into categories.
Numbered bold front: a bold line like **1. front** starts a card; the lines below it are the answer.
Q:/A: format: a Q: line is the front; the first A: line is the answer, and any lines after it become a second paragraph.
Within an answer, consecutive lines join into one paragraph; leave a blank line to start a new paragraph.
Example deck:

"# Spanish Basics
*A starter deck*

## Greetings

**1. hola**
hello

**2. buenos días**
good morning
Used until about noon.

## Numbers

Q: uno
A: one

Q: dos
A: two"
Branching decks

Turn a deck into a choose-your-path sequence instead of a plain review. Give a card a name with a line like [cave] just above its question, then add options below it as a line starting with a dash, ending in an arrow to another card\'s name, for example: Sneak past -> treasure. A card with no options is a normal, dead-end card.
Open the branching deck guide →
Studying & spaced repetition
Spaced repetition (SM-2)

flashkarte schedules reviews with the SM-2 algorithm. Every card has a due date. Cards rated highly move further into the future; cards you struggle with come back sooner — often the next day. The goal is to see each card right before you would otherwise forget it, so review sessions stay short.
The rating buttons
After flipping a card, rate how well you recalled it. This is what schedules the next review — be honest, not optimistic.
Again — you did not recall it. The card resets and comes back tomorrow.
Hard — you recalled it, but it was a struggle. The next interval grows by less than Good.
Good — you recalled it correctly with reasonable effort. The interval grows at the normal pace.
Easy — recalling it felt effortless. The interval grows more than Good.
Perfect — instant, effortless recall. The interval grows the most.
Multiple-choice mode
Switch to Choice mode during a session to get answer options built automatically from your other cards — you are graded the moment you tap one.
Creating decks with AI
An AI assistant can build decks for you and push them straight into your account, using your own AI account — flashkarte\'s server never runs the AI itself.
In Settings, generate an API key and copy the MCP server URL.
Add the URL as a custom connector in your AI client (for example claude.ai or Claude Desktop) and sign in with your flashkarte account.
Ask it to build a deck, for example: Turn this into a flashkarte deck: … — the new deck appears in your account, ready to study.
Sharing & exploring
Making a deck public
Publish one of your decks from its menu to get a shareable link and have it listed in the Library for others to find. You can unpublish it again at any time.
Library
Search public decks shared by other flashkarte users and clone any of them straight into your account to start studying immediately.
New here? Open Help to learn the basics.
Not sure what these do? See how spaced repetition works in Help.
